chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Bilāl, who said:

I wrote to him concerning making up the supererogatory prayer from the rising of dawn until the rising of the sun, and from after al-ʿAṣr until the sun sets. So he wrote: That is not permissible except for the one who is making it up; as for someone other than him, then no.

key_terms.بَعْدِ الْعَصْرِ: the time after the ʿAṣr prayer
key_terms.قَضَاءِ: making up a missed act of worship
key_terms.لِلْمُقْتَضِي: for the one making up what was missed

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform qaḍāʾ of missed nafilah prayers between dawn and sunrise or after al-ʿAṣr before sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on making up missed supererogatory prayers during times generally discouraged for prayer: from dawn until sunrise and after al-ʿAṣr until sunset. It states that such prayer is permitted only for one making up a missed nafilah, and not for others.
